Introduction

Verbal Jint, born Kim Jin‑tae, is a South Korean rapper, producer, and musician. The origin of his stage name is a combination of the character Roger "Verbal" Kint from the 1995 film 'The Usual Suspects', and his birth name, Jin-tae.

Verbal Jint first appeared in the late 90's, at a time when hip-hop was considered a dangerous trend in South Korea. He performed as a member of the underground hip‑hop crew Show N Prove (SNP), releasing solo tracks like “Big Brag” and “How High School”, which cemented his presence in the underground scene. Before his solo debut, Korean rap largely relied on fast delivery and repetitive rhythms without true rhyme schemes. Verbal Jint disrupted that norm by introducing grammatically precise rhymes in Korean, a move that revolutionized the genre and became the new standard. The EP Modern Rhymes (2001) is still considered to be the blueprint of Korean rap and because of this, he is referred to as the 'Godfather of Korean hip‑hop'.

Academically, Verbal Jint holds an economics degree from Seoul National University, and later enrolled at Hanyang University School of Law, though he paused his legal studies to focus on music. He also served as an army sergeant through the KATUSA program despite being exempt, choosing to serve alongside U.S. forces.

His 2008 album 'Framed' earned Best Hip‑Hop Album at the Korean Music Awards, marking his first major industry recognition. He signed with Brand New Music in 2010, and released the album 'Go Easy' the following year. Its single “You Look Good” became a major hit, climbing to No. 5 on the Gaon Digital Chart. In 2012, his album '10 Years of  Misinterpretation' spawned hits like “Good Morning” (featuring 10 cm) and “Pretty Enough,” both landing in the Gaon top 10.

Verbal Jint appeared on the very first season of Show Me the Money in 2012, returned as a mentor/producer in Show Me the Money 4 (2015), and also participated in the spin‑off Unpretty Rapstar, producing singles for contestants. In 2015, he released both the EP 'Yeoja' with Sanchez and the album 'GO HARD Pt. 1: The Other Side'.

In 2010, he began releasing music under Brand New Stardom, a record label owned by rappers Cho PD and Rhymer. When the company split in two in 2011, Verbal Jint followed Rhymer to his new label Brand New Music. In November 2015, Brand New Music announced that he had launched his independent label OTHERSIDE under their umbrella, aiming to explore “the other side” of his artistry.

Beyond music, Verbal Jint is also a sought‑after voiceover artist, lending his distinctive voice to commercials for brands like Vitamin Water, LG, and Hyundai.

He has collaborated with many artists of various genres including Taeyeon ('I'), Davichi, Cho Yong-pil, Dynamic Duo, Ailee, Beenzino, 10cm and many more.
